summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder with chronic indwelling Foley catheter, type 2 diabetes, and foot ulcer s/p left TMA was admitted for diffuse abdominal pain and left flank pain. Evaluation revealed a complicated urinary tract infection due to E. coli and significant fecal loading causing constipation. She was treated with IV antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral cefpodoxime for a 14-day course. Her abdominal pain improved after disimpaction and bowel regimen optimization. Due to persistently elevated blood glucose levels in the 200s–400s, her Lantus insulin was increased from 10 to 20 units at bedtime. The central line placed for IV access was removed prior to discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor blood sugar, and maintain bowel and wound care routines.
